jobs.title: Director of Quality
jobs.description_text: Position Overview We're looking for a Director of Quality to build our quality function from the ground up — including our path toward ISO 9001 — and lead it for the long haul. This role sets the multi-year quality strategy while staying grounded in what's really happening on the floor, in the supply base, and with customers. Our hardware matters; defects here aren't abstract metrics. Our core philosophy is quality at the source: quality can't be inspected in after the fact, it has to be built right the first time. QA is the backstop, not the primary defense — an escape that reaches the customer is a production failure, not a QA failure. We want a pragmatic leader who favors simple, practical problem-solving (5 Whys, direct observation) over paperwork-heavy processes, and who will build a genuine partnership with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers to catch issues at the source rather than at receiving. What You'll Do: Strategic & Long-Range Leadership Own the long-range quality strategy, translating business goals into a multi-year plan for systems, staffing, and capability. Architect our Quality Management System — including our path toward ISO 9001 — from the ground up, building processes that are clear and simple, not just audit-ready. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE As Bedrock scales deployments nationwide, every machine we bring autonomy to has to be vetted, provisioned, calibrated, deployed, monitored, updated and serviced. Fleet Engineering builds the platform behind that lifecycle: the system of record, services and applications that teams across Bedrock use to run a fleet growing to thousands of machines. Many of these systems will be used by external partners as well. The work crosses disciplines. One week you're architecting how we track sensor calibrations across every machine. The next, you're making a fault on an operator's tablet readable at a glance. You'll own problems end to end, working closely with technicians and operators in the field as well as multidisciplinary engineers across hardware, ML and robotics. Also, you get to drive 100,000 lb excavators. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the fleet system of record: the data model and services for machines, their hardware, worksites and deployments, and how each moves through its lifecycle - Build the applications that technicians, dispatchers and operations teams use every day to vet machines, schedule installs, track inventory and keep the fleet healthy - Build the services every robot phones home to: delivering identity, credentials, calibrations and configuration to machines in the field, and always knowing what's running where - Move petabytes of sensor data off remote job sites across the country, bringing home the real-world data that powers our ML and learning fly

jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for an exceptional Technical Artist to join our team building and scaling our robotics simulation environment. Simulation is a critical foundation for autonomy at Bedrock—it allows us to validate end-to-end systems, evaluate complex and unsafe scenarios, and run testing at massive scale. Our autonomy stack is deeply machine-learning–driven, and closing the sim-to-real gap is a core focus of this role. The simulator must accurately represent a living, breathing construction site - real-world lighting, 3D content, and terrain deformation for digging and earthmoving - while remaining efficient enough to support thousands of runs. High-quality simulation directly accelerates robotics development, making this work central to our success. jobs.title: 2027 Internship Simulation Engineer, Neural Rendering
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Before an autonomous excavator digs its first trench on a new site, it's already dug thousands in simulation. The Simulation team builds the virtual environments our autonomy stack trains and tests against — and the closer sim looks and behaves like the real world, the faster we move. Neural rendering is the next step: replacing hand-authored assets and approximations with learned representations that capture the visual complexity of real jobsites — dust, lighting, deformable terrain, heavy equipment in motion. As our Simulation intern, you'll push neural rendering techniques into our sim pipeline and measure whether they actually close the visual gap that matters for downstream autonomy performance. jobs.title: 2027 Internship Behavior ML Engineer, Learned Manipulation Policies
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Teaching a 40-ton excavator to move like an expert operator is a very different problem from teaching a car to stay in its lane. The motions are multimodal, there are many good ways to swing, dig, and dump and the consequences of getting them wrong are measured in cubic yards and bent steel. Bedrock's Behavior ML team builds the learned policies that decide what our machines actually do, and diffusion policies are a central bet: models that can represent the full distribution of expert behavior instead of averaging it into mush. As our Behavior ML intern, you'll help train those policies and build the evaluation that tells us whether they're genuinely better working alongside two hosts who sit on both the training and evaluation sides of the problem. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Train and iterate on diffusion flow matching, and related behavior policies using real fleet demonstration data and simulated rollouts - Run architecture, conditioning, and hyperparameter explorations, and turn the results into clear findings the team can build on - Build and improve evaluation pipelines that score behavior models on task success, smoothness, safety margins, and operator-likeness - Investigate failure modes - distribution shift, mode collapse, out-of-distribution scenes and propose fixes - Work with the simulation and eval teams to make sure offline metrics actually predict on-machine performance - Contribute to the shared training codebase with clean, reviewed, reproducible

jobs.description_text: Bedrock Robotics, Inc. seeks a Hardware Engineer in San Francisco, CA responsible for designing, manufacturing, and testing its autonomous hardware systems, including high performance computer systems, sensors, controllers, interfaces to machines, and testing equipment. This position will work with autonomous hardware systems installed on standard heavy construction machinery—excavators, bulldozers, and wheel loaders—to allow that equipment to perform earthmoving work on construction sites autonomously. In this context, “autonomous hardware systems” are the physical electronic components installed on a construction machine that allow it to operate without a human operator in the cab. They consist of: high-performance computer systems (ruggedized onboard computers mounted on the machine that perform the calculations required for autonomous operation); sensors (devices that allow the machine to perceive its surroundings, including cameras, radar, lidar, and GNSS); controllers and interfaces (electronic units that translate the computer's decisions into electrical signals that operate the machine's existing hydraulic, steering, and engine controls); and testing equipment (benches, fixtures, and instrumentation used to verify each of the above components before and after installation on a machine). You will work closely with manufacturing engineers, warehouse associates, global supply managers, truck drivers, and quality engineers to build intuitive, reliable tools for controlling and understanding material movement. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Set the pace: Move quickly, make decisions with imperfect information, and take responsibility for outcomes. You help the team operate with clarity and urgency. - Own critical tools: Design, build, and operate core services that power our Austin factory. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base works in the physical world. A homeowner finds us and decides to trust a new kind of power company. A crew installs the battery. The city approves it, the utility connects it, and we dispatch it, telling it when to charge and when to send power back based on local grid conditions and the member’s usage. Launching a market means learning all of that fast, building software that works there, and then doing it again in the next state. Then you’ll build whatever it takes to make the launch work, from a partner’s spreadsheet to BaseOS to the firmware on the battery. jobs.title: Industrial IT Support Specialist
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a hands-on, customer-focused IT Support Specialist to join our factory IT team at Base. You’ll help keep our flagship battery factory (BF1) and warehouse network running around the clock. You’ll be the first point of contact for factory and warehouse IT issues, managing tickets and walk-ups while troubleshooting technology directly on the production floor. This hands-on role includes racking switches, calibrating label printers, provisioning scanners, and resolving issues that could bring production stations to a halt. This is a designated second-shift role. You must be available to work Monday through Friday, 3 p.m. to 12 a.m. Your assigned shift will depend on team coverage needs and may change as the company and team grow. This role will require periodic travel to our facilities across Texas and, as we expand, other states. You’ll primarily support factory and warehouse operations but will also provide IT support to the broader company as needed. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Provide hands-on technical support across factory and warehouse operations, including laptops, workstations, handheld scanners, label printers, kiosks, time clocks, badge printers, and production-adjacent systems. - Deploy, configure, and maintain Zebra hardware across all locations, including wireless barcode scanners, charging docks, and thermal transfer label printers. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base is looking for a Real Estate Analyst to join our team to help build and run our physical footprint. Every new market we launch starts with a building — a distribution warehouse to stage and service batteries, and eventually manufacturing and office space to grow into. Today that footprint spans a manufacturing campus in Austin, a distribution network across multiple states, and a headquarters. On every deal, you work with the teams who will use the building to scope what they actually need, then source the options, underwrite them, and negotiate the deal through a certificate of occupancy. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. - 1+ years designing and running tests on electrical equipment. - Experience working around lithium-ion batteries, high voltage, and DAQ systems. - Comfort with hands-on, mostly outdoor work. PREFERRED SKILLS - Battery thermal runaway testing. - UL 9540, UL 9540A, or UL 1973. - Short circuit or other high-energy testing. - Fixture and test setup design in CAD. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE When Base hardware fails in the field, it comes back to you. You'll open it up, run the tests, and help engineers figure out exactly what broke and why. Your findings feed directly into design changes, firmware fixes, and line improvements on a product already running in homes. jobs.description_text: We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient. Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships. You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code. jobs.title: Manager, Build Engineering
jobs.description_text: Role Summary Hadrian is looking for a Manager, Build Engineering to lead the team that takes new products from zero to one on a dedicated customer program. You will own new product introduction end-to-end — from first article through qualification, ramp, and transition into standard production — and be accountable for the build outcomes of every engineer on your team. This role sits at the center of the factory's cross-functional web. A new product doesn't reach one without Supply Chain, Capability Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Software, Materials & Processes, and Test all pulling in the same direction, and it's on you to keep those dependencies from becoming your engineers' problem to solve build by build. You will own the relationship expectations between your program's Build Engineers and every function that supports them, resolving constraints before they hit the floor. You will set one standard for how build plans, process definitions, and work instructions are written across all three commodities. Decisions made during NPI set the cost, lead time, and quality of these parts for their life, and the processes your team introduces become capabilities Hadrian uses on the programs that follow. jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: This person leads execution of Hadrian’s capital markets activity, with a primary emphasis on debt capital markets. They will translate Hadrian’s operational and financial needs (new factories, machine capex, working capital, and growth) into well-structured, executable financing transactions across both corporate and asset-backed contexts, and drive those transactions from structuring through diligence, negotiation, and close. They will own relationships with banks, private credit funds, and other debt capital providers, and partner closely with the CFO, SVP of Capital Markets, Treasury, FP&A, and Legal to align financing strategy with liquidity planning, capital allocation, and long-term planning. The role is explicitly outward-facing and execution-focused, operates comfortably in non-standard situations where Hadrian’s model does not fit traditional corporate lending frameworks, and will grow into building out the capital markets function as Hadrian’s financing cadence scales. What You’ll Do - Lead end-to-end execution of debt transactions (credit facilities, term loans, private credit, equipment and facility financing, and structured debt) from initial structuring through diligence, negotiation, and closing. - Structure financing solutions across corporate and asset-backed contexts, tailored to Hadrian’s operating model, including equipment finance, receivables facilities, sale-leasebacks, project-level debt, and government-backed loans. - Own lender engagement

You will work closely with engineers to turn designs into safe, dependable production systems of the future. jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hadrian is building a team that converts decades-old technical data, scanned and hand-marked prints and the requirements behind them, into model-based definition. Hadrian's software does much of the conversion, and engineers review and complete what it produces. As a Manufacturing Engineer, MBD, you do this work by hand on the hardest packages. What you learn shapes the software and the process the team runs on. Senior engineers in this role set the definition standard and work with the software team on what the tool must handle. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Work through customer packages across welding, assembly, NDT, and machining requirements, and author them onto the model as linked MBD. - Review what Hadrian's software produces, correct it, and report each class of error to the software team. - Help define the standard workflow and its quality checks, so a larger team can run the work in the software. - Review other engineers' output against the definition standard. - Train the engineers and specialists who join the team. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 3+ years of industry experience in CAD modeling, with work centered on drawings and product definition: MBD authoring, drawing checking, or legacy-data conversion. - Reads messy legacy prints across welding, assembly, NDT, and machining callouts, including weld and NDT symbols per AWS A2.4, and resolves ambiguity against the specifications and engineering reports the print references. - GD&T to ASME Y14.5 and MBD/PMI to Y14.41, eno

jobs.title: Administrative Assistant, Office of the CEO

jobs.description_text: THE ROLE We are in search of senior sales and customer business development professionals with the drive to build strong, value-driven relationships with market leaders that support our growth objectives. This role reports to the Director of Sales and calls for an experienced strategic enterprise seller — someone with a substantial track record in high-level, strategic sales roles at manufacturing companies who embraces the value of planning, process, and execution against company and customer goals. jobs.title: Growth Finance Manager
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Growth Finance owns the economics of how Hadrian wins work. We sit at the front end of every program — pricing the pursuit, shaping the deal, and structuring the partnerships and joint ventures that get new capacity off the ground with our commercial and government customers. The Associate is the analytical center of that work. You'll build the model behind a pursuit from a blank sheet: unit economics, capacity and capex requirements, rate and margin structure, and the returns case that determines whether we bid, at what price, and on what terms. You'll pressure-test your own assumptions before anyone else gets the chance, and you'll be expected to have a view — not just a spreadsheet — on whether a program is worth pursuing. Beyond the model, you'll help structure the vehicles. That means partnership and JV economics, term sheets, waterfall and downside mechanics, and the diligence behind counterparties we're considering taking risk with. You'll write the memo that goes to leadership, and you'll defend it in the room. This is a small team with a short path to owning deals outright. The work available to you scales with what you demonstrate rather than with tenure. You will work directly with the executive leadership team at Hadrian on some of the company’s most important strategic initiatives. jobs.title: Site Security Manager
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hadrian's Physical Security team protects the people, factories and export-controlled work behind Hadrian's growth. As we open new factories and bring on new teams, every site needs a security leader on the ground, and the program needs people who help build it across all of our sites. You will own security at our Torrance campus and be hands on every day: managing the contract security team, walking the site, and acting as the first call for any security risk. This is more than a walk-the-floor role. You'll also own a program area across every Hadrian site, such as investigations, workplace violence prevention, vendor management or security training, and help build a physical security program that keeps pace with the business. You'll partner with site leadership, Facilities, EH&S, People and the Facility Security Officer, and report to the Director of Physical Security. This is an on-site role in Torrance, CA. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Manage the contract security vendor at the site: set post orders and patrol plans, check the work against them, and hold the vendor to the contract. - Walk the site regularly, find gaps in doors, openings and day-to-day security practice, rank them, and get them fixed. - Lead the response to security incidents and site events as the first security leader on scene, and document them clearly. - Keep site controls in place, including badge access, visitor management, key control, contractor escorts and controlled areas, in partnership with the Fa

jobs.title: Security Systems & Technology Lead
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian's Physical Security team protects the people, factories and export-controlled work behind Hadrian's growth. We are opening new factories and facilities at a rapid pace, and every one of them needs security systems designed, built and commissioned to a single standard, so each new site is a standard package and not a new project. You will own the technology behind Hadrian's physical security program: access control, video surveillance and the systems around them, from security input on construction drawings through installation, commissioning and day-to-day administration. You'll set the standards, run several site builds and platform migrations at the same time, and hold integrators to the work. You'll partner closely with IT, Facilities, Information Security and the Facility Security Officer, and report to the Director of Physical Security. This is an individual contributor role based on site in Torrance, CA, San Francisco, CA or Mesa, AZ, with travel up to 30% to Hadrian sites. jobs.title: Build Engineer, Large Scale Machining
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian is looking for a Build Engineer, Large Scale Machining to own how our largest machined parts get made, including castings, forgings, plate weldments, and hull-scale structures. You will own each part from the first design review through qualification, ramp, and handoff to standard production. You are the bridge between the product and Capability Engineering: you interpret the product requirements, drive DFM, establish the build flow and sequence, and hand Capability Engineering a well-defined machining problem to solve. You will own new product and new process introduction for large machined parts end-to-end. Large parts are where precision gets hard: tight features are spread across multiple setups, and a datum scheme has to survive stress relief, flips, and weld. You set how each part flows through the factory, define the machining processes it needs, and work across Design, Supply Chain, Capability Engineering, Tooling, Quality, and Operations to bring it to rate. Decisions made during NPI set the cost, lead time, and quality of these parts for their life, and the processes you introduce become large-format machining capabilities Hadrian uses on the programs that follow. This role sits on the Build Engineering Commodities team alongside sheet metal and tube and pipe. It is hands-on. You will be at the machine for first parts, and you will own the outcome. jobs.title: Build Engineer, Castings
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian is looking for a Build Engineer, Castings to own large structural castings from the first design review through qualification, ramp, and handoff to standard production, whether we pour them, buy them, or run both paths in parallel. You are the bridge between the product and Capability Engineering: you interpret the product requirements, drive DFM, reverse engineer the product where the data is incomplete, establish the build flow and sequence, and hand Capability Engineering and the foundry a well-defined casting problem to solve. You will own new product and new process introduction for castings end-to-end. Many of the hardest products we build start as a casting, and decisions made at the pattern carry through machining, weld, and final assembly. You set how each casting is made and inspected, define the processes it needs, and work across Design, Supply Chain, supplier foundries, Capability Engineering, Quality, and Operations to bring it to rate. Decisions made during NPI set the cost, lead time, and quality of these castings for their life, and the processes you introduce become casting capabilities Hadrian uses on the programs that follow. They lead integration across every functional workstream, from diligence and pre-close planning through Day 1, Day 100, and the transition to business-as-usual. They translate deal theses into concrete workplans, governance, and milestones; coordinate functional leaders across Operations, Finance, HR, IT, Legal, Quality, Supply Chain, and EHS; and keep the business, its customers, and its mission running without disruption throughout. They own integration workstreams end to end under the direction of corp dev / strategy leadership, working alongside FP&A, Engineering, Operations, and Legal to keep integration aligned with the broader business. The role sits at the intersection of strategy, operations, and the defense / advanced-manufacturing market, and scales as the corp dev function and deal cadence grow. Your job is to run Strategic Comms with full ownership of its craft and its team. jobs.description_text: Role Summary The Director, Forward Deployed Engineering leads the technical arm of Hadrian's Customer Programs motion. You sit inside Build Engineering and partner directly with the Customer Programs team, owning the manufacturing scoping of new customer engagements: translating what a customer wants into what Hadrian will actually commit to and build. This role works directly with customers every day. For many of them, you and your team are the face of Hadrian engineering, so how you show up in the room matters as much as the technical answer. The work starts with discovery. Before anything is proposed, you and your team get inside the customer's operation: observing how work actually flows, mapping their processes and constraints, and interviewing the people closest to the problem until you understand what they need, which is often different from what they first ask for. From there, you shape a solution that maximizes what the customer gets out of the engagement and builds toward where Hadrian is headed. The craft is steering to the answer where the customer's best outcome and Hadrian's direction reinforce each other: high impact, low effort, and built on what we already do well rather than new obligations we then have to invent our way out of. jobs.title: CAD Modeler
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: US defense systems run on technical data that is often decades old: scanned paper, hand-marked prints, partial models, and drawings that were never turned into 3D models. A part that exists only on an old drawing is hard to source. That slows how fast the armed forces and our prime customers can sustain and rebuild the systems that use it. Hadrian turns that data into manufacturing-ready models and drawings, so customers can keep their systems running and Hadrian can make or procure the parts. As a CAD Modeler, you build the 3D models and 2D drawings for naval and aerospace parts, starting from whatever the customer sends. You also build the models and drawings for each manufacturing state (M-state) of a part: the in-process configurations the factory builds and inventories on the way to the final part. Our engineers define each M-state, and you model, draw, and configure it. You own your parts from first model through release and every change after it. When fully operational you’ll support manufacturing technicians in the use of Hadrian’s proprietary AI platform Opus. You’ll act as a bridge between the customer and product providing valuable feedback directly from the factory floor to help further refine and develop the platform. As we scale, the People team plays a critical role in shaping how we attract, enable, and retain world-class talent across both engineering and advanced manufacturing. Working on the People team at Hadrian means designing and operationalizing the foundation of a company that blends cutting-edge robotics, AI, and precision manufacturing — while supporting a workforce that spans software engineers, machinists, program managers, and everything in between. In this highly cross-functional role, you'll own the end-to-end delivery of critical people programs - while building the systems, processes, and structures that keep our team aligned, accountable, and moving fast. Our goal is to accelerate the maturity and operational effectiveness of Hadrian's factories through targeted training programs. The team is responsible for developing and managing a comprehensive training system, driving software adoption, standardizing operational processes, and maintaining an integrated training and certification ecosystem. Before our first technicians arrive, you will go through their onboarding and training yourself, test it, and help us refine it so the people who follow have the best possible start. Manufacturing experience is a bonus, and you will learn our production environment through time at our sites in Los Angeles and Arizona and through equipment manufacturer training. jobs.title: Internal Communications & Knowledge Systems Partner
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: Hadrian is growing fast, and how we share knowledge, make decisions, and communicate is as much a part of what we’re building as anything on the factory floor. We’re looking for an Internal Communications Partner who sees the organization itself as a product, with every employee as a user, and wants to help design how it works. You’re AI forward by default. You’ll think about internal content the way a great product team thinks about product documentation: built around real users, held to a high quality bar, and always current. You’ll shape how information gets created, found, and kept up to date across the company, and set the standards and systems everyone else builds on. This is a chance to define what great looks like from the ground up, at a company where the pace and the stakes are high. jobs.description_text: Role Overview We are hiring Piping Design Engineers to rebuild how piping design is done. Piping is one of the largest cost and schedule drivers in a refinery, and one of the least automated disciplines in engineering. The workflow has barely changed in thirty years: someone routes a line by hand in a 3D model, someone else checks it by eye, and the quantities get counted downstream after the fact. The tooling available today, modeling software, geometry and CAD APIs, and modern AI coding assistants, has moved far enough that a large share of that work should be generated, checked, and optimized by software. That is the job. You will do the real design work including layout, routing, supports, stress, isometrics, quantities. And then go after the parts of it that should never have been manual. You will write the checks, build the scripts, and stand up the workflows that let a small team model a plant that would normally take an army of designers. What You’ll Do - Build the 3D model.
